security_justification.audit_integrity: The sink sends exactly the validated event bytes and reports acceptance only for the one exact acknowledgment, so no field is rewritten and no failure becomes a delivered state.
security_justification.authentication_or_authorization: The sink holds no credential of its own; caller headers go only to the configured origin, and distribution needs the owner's merge of the evaluation authorization.
security_justification.authority_provenance: The authoritativeTenant union only narrows a type; branding, runtime validation and the authority registry are unchanged, and client claims stay distinct from authoritative values.
security_justification.concurrency: Concurrent emits are allowed with no ordering promise; each request is independent and settles once, and flush tracks only requests started before it.
security_justification.confidentiality: Events go only to the configured origin with no redirect following, headers are never logged or echoed, and the outcome callback never receives bodies, payloads or header values.
security_justification.cryptography: No cryptography is implemented; https origins use the runtime's TLS, and the kit identity uses SHA-256 digests for identification, not for trust.
security_justification.error_disclosure: Core sink-failure diagnostics keep F-11's bounded fields with no event identifier; the callback reports only the event identifier, a closed code and a status.
security_justification.external_security_integration: The sink reaches only the configured origin through the governed fetch adapter and adds no dependency; the kit gate fetches pinned tools from the npm registry only at gate time.
security_justification.fail_posture: Invalid sink options throw at construction, every ambiguous response maps to failure rather than acceptance, and the kit gate fails closed, including when the registry is unreachable.
security_justification.lifecycle: flush waits for in-flight requests and SDK shutdown drains within its bound before closing the sink; emits after shutdown return SDK_SHUT_DOWN.
security_justification.mutation_ownership: Changes are confined to the exact paths in owned_paths and the two canonical Node and core capability specs through the fold; no CB-018-owned or governance-core path is touched.
security_justification.privacy_transformation: No field is transformed by the sink; the evaluation is synthetic-data only, with a stop-and-purge condition if non-synthetic data reaches a receiver.
security_justification.resource_retention: The sink retains only the set of in-flight requests; responses are read to the adapter's bound and discarded, and the kit is written only outside the repository.
security_justification.retry_or_redelivery: The sink never retries, batches or queues; one attempt per emit is the documented guarantee, and correlation.retry_attempt is sent exactly as validated.
security_justification.trust_boundary: The receiving peer is untrusted; the shared classifier reduces its behaviour to a closed code set, and the example receiver re-runs full SDK validation instead of trusting structure.
